How we run Meta ads for a practice

  • 1. Pick the treatments that suit social

    Not everything belongs on Instagram, and pretending it does wastes money.

    Cosmetic, ortho and high value treatments get Meta campaigns, because people mull those over and scroll while they do. Emergency and check-ups stay on Google, where people search when they need you now.

  • 2. Shoot the creative at your clinic

    A stock photo of a stranger's smile tells a patient nothing about you.

    On day five of our first week, we create video and stills at your practice: your rooms, your team, your front desk. So when someone finally walks in, it already looks familiar.

  • 3. Show it to the right people nearby

    Patients book close to home, so the ads stay close to home too.

    We build audiences around your area and your real patient base, then retarget people who've already looked at your site. Someone who read your Invisalign page last week sees your Invisalign ad this week.

  • 4. Catch every lead the moment it lands

    Meta leads go cold faster than any other kind. They tapped a form between two videos and moved on.

    Lead forms and Instagram DMs all go into SmileOX, our own lead platform. It replies in under 60 seconds, asks the questions your team would ask, scores the lead hot, warm or cool, and runs a 14-day follow-up for the people not ready yet. See how SmileOX works.

  • 5. Written to AHPRA's rules

    Every ad is checked against the AHPRA advertising guidelines before it runs.

    No testimonials about clinical care, nothing that sets up unreasonable expectations, and no offers without clear terms. Social ads get shared and screenshotted, so getting this right matters even more.

  • 6. Judged on booked patients

    Likes and reach are easy to buy. They don't pay for a chair.

    We track which campaigns turn into booked appointments, then look at the numbers with you on a call every fortnight and move the budget to what's working.

Meta or Google Ads?

Straight answer: they do different jobs.

Search catches patients who have already decided. Social creates the decision.

That's why cosmetic and ortho belong on Instagram, and emergency doesn't. Most of our clients run both: Google for the people searching today, Meta for the people who'll be ready in a month. How we run Google Ads for dentists.

Where the ads send people

The ad is only the start.

Someone who taps an ad for clear aligners and lands on your homepage usually leaves.

So every campaign sends people to a page about the treatment they were shown, with a simple way to book or ask a question. If those pages don't exist yet, we build them. More on dental websites.

Straight answers

Questions dentists ask about Facebook and Instagram ads.

Do Facebook and Instagram ads work for dentists?

Yes, for the right treatments. They work best for things people think about before they book, like cosmetic work, ortho and other high value treatments. For a toothache at 7am, Google is where people go, so that budget belongs in search.

Should I run Meta ads or Google Ads?

Usually both, doing different jobs. Search catches patients who have already decided. Social is where the deciding happens. We put each treatment where its patients actually are.

Do I need professional video for my ads?

You need real video, not stock. We shoot the creative at your clinic, so the ad looks like your practice and your team. That happens on day five of our first week with you.

What happens when someone fills in a Meta lead form?

It goes straight into SmileOX, along with Instagram DMs. SmileOX replies in under 60 seconds, asks the questions your team would ask, and keeps following up with the ones who aren't ready yet.

Can my ads include a special offer?

Only with clear terms. AHPRA's advertising rules don't allow offers without them, and we check every ad against those rules before it runs.

Will you run Meta ads for my competitor?

Not if they're a dental practice within 7km of you.
